subject: Game Theory
title: Power Indices
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Power Indices.

hook.text: Luxembourg had 2 votes in the 1958 EU Council. Germany had 4. But Luxembourg's power was actually zero.

buildup.text: Power indices measure a player's ability to change outcomes—not their raw vote share.

discovery.text: The Banzhaf index counts how often a voter is pivotal: removing them changes the result from winning to losing.

twist.text: A player with 49% of votes can have zero power if 51% always votes together. Size isn't power.

climax.text: Power indices redesigned the EU voting system to better reflect population and actual influence.

punchline.text: Power is about pivotality, not size.

quiz.question: What does the Banzhaf power index measure?
options: How often a voter is pivotal to the outcome
